To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The Vector Space Model (or any model that is based on it) is not suitable for information retrieval in context.
the ranking of documents is sensitive to the context in which they are generated.

• the notion of basis of the vector space is introduced to represent context, • the notion of subspace is used to describe context and • the notion of distance between a document vector and the space spanned by the basis is used to rank in context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of retrieval and ranking in context.
ranking in context, where context is defined in terms of a set of versors.
the problem of retrieval of documents in context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ranking function proposed in this paper ranks documents in context.

the ranking of a query vector x in a context B is given by a distance between x and L(B) and is defined as d(x, L(B)) = min y∈L(B) |x − y| = min y∗ |x − y∗ |, where y∗ = p∗ · B, p∗ ∈ R k and p∗ is such that y∗ ∈ L(B).
the proposed approach to context-sensitive retrieval is based on the notion of basis of the vector space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide the first formal definition of a context and the first formal description of a context-based ranking algorithm.
we have developed a new model for ranking in context.
we have shown that the VSM is not a model of context and we have proposed an alternative model that is sensitive to it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the basis is a fundamental concept to understand context and ranking in context.
a document vector should not be generated by a fixed basis, which is a set of versors.
a basis is a way of describing context, which is a set of pieces of context.
